# Overweight and obesity

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Endocrinology > Disorders of glucose metabolism > Overweight and obesity*

[Original Article Link](/library/4g03v2)

---

## Summary

<u>Overweight</u> and <u>obesity</u> are characterized by an accumulation of excess body fat (adiposity) associated with the risk of developing <u>weight-related complications</u>. Multiple underlying factors (e.g., genetics, hormonal changes, lifestyle behaviors, medical conditions, medication use) ultimately result in prolonged excess energy intake relative to <u>energy expenditure</u>. <u>Body mass index</u> (<u>BMI</u>) and <u>waist circumference</u> are used to diagnose and classify <u>overweight</u> and <u>obesity</u> and to estimate the risk of <u>weight-related complications</u>. Clinical evaluation and diagnostic studies are used to assess for contributing <u>causes of overweight and obesity</u> and <u>weight-related complications</u> (e.g., <u>hypertension</u>, cardiovascular disease, <u>dyslipidemia</u>, <u>diabetes</u>), and a <u>clinical severity assessment of obesity</u> should be performed. Management focuses on weight loss and preventing or improving <u>weight-related complications</u> and should be individualized based on <u>shared decision-making</u>. Management options include lifestyle changes (dietary changes, increased physical activity, and/or behavioral interventions), pharmacotherapy, and <u>bariatric surgery</u>. Interventions are often performed concurrently.

---

## Classification

### <u>Body mass index</u> [[7]](/library/iKXJT_)[[8]](/library/2udTq70)[[9]](/library/3udSI70)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)




Lower cutoffs for <u>BMI</u> are used in individuals of Asian descent.  [[7]](/library/iKXJT_)[[8]](/library/2udTq70)[[9]](/library/3udSI70)[[11]](/library/iudJI70)




| <br>BMI classification for overweight and obesity [[7]](/library/iKXJT_)[[8]](/library/2udTq70)[[9]](/library/3udSI70)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)<br> |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  | <br>Adults (absolute <u>BMI</u>) | <br>Children aged 2–17 years (<u>BMI</u> <u>percentile</u> for age and sex)   [[4]](/library/Fmdghq0)[[12]](/library/VaWGjP0)<br> |
| <u>Overweight</u> |  |  |  |  | <br><br>* Most populations: 25–29.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup><br><br>* Asian descent: 23–24.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup>   [[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[14]](/library/aydQds0)<br><br><br> | <br>* 85th–94th <u>percentile</u><br><br> |
| <u>Class 1 obesity</u> |  |  |  |  | <br><br>* Most populations: 30–34.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup><br><br>* Asian descent: 25–29.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup>   [[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[14]](/library/aydQds0)<br><br><br> | <br>* 100–119% of the 95th <u>percentile</u><br><br> |
| <u>Class 2 obesity</u> |  |  |  |  | <br><br>* Most populations: 35–39.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup><br><br>* Asian descent: 30–34.9 kg/m<sup>2</sup><br><br><br> | <br>* 120–139% of the 95th <u>percentile</u><br><br> |
| <u>Class 3 obesity</u> |  |  |  |  | <br><br>* Most populations: ≥ 40 kg/m<sup>2</sup><br><br>* Asian descent: ≥ 35 kg/m<sup>2</sup><br><br><br> | <br>* ≥ 140% of the 95th <u>percentile</u><br><br> |





> [!TIP]
> There is a direct relationship between increasing <u>BMI</u> and increasing risk of <u>ASCVD</u>, <u>type 2 diabetes</u> (<u>T2DM</u>), and <u>all-cause mortality</u>. [[15]](/library/QKXuT_)




> [!TIP]
> To determine class 2 or <u>class 3 obesity</u> in children, use the adult <u>BMI</u> cutoff if it is lower than the pediatric <u>BMI</u> <u>percentile</u> for age and sex cutoff. [[4]](/library/Fmdghq0)

### Clinical severity




In patients with confirmed <u>obesity</u>, use a clinical severity classification system for <u>obesity</u> for risk <u>stratification</u>.




#### American Association of Clinical <u>Endocrinology</u> [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)




* Stage 1 <u>obesity</u>: no <u>weight-related complications</u>

* Stage 2 <u>obesity</u>: ≥ 1 <u>weight-related complication</u> of mild to moderate severity

* Stage 3 <u>obesity</u>: ≥ 1 severe <u>weight-related complication</u>





> [!TIP]
> The severity of each <u>weight-related complication</u> should be determined on an individual basis and based on clinical judgement. [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)




#### Lancet <u>Diabetes</u> and <u>Endocrinology</u> Commission [[16]](/library/rCdftH0)




* Preclinical <u>obesity</u>: excess adiposity without the features of clinical <u>obesity</u>

* Clinical <u>obesity</u> diagnostic criteria

* Organ or tissue dysfunction due to <u>obesity</u>

* AND/OR substantial limitation of <u>ADLs</u> due to <u>obesity</u>

---

## Clinical features

* Characteristic findings [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)

* Increased <u>BMI</u>

* Increased <u>waist circumference</u>

* Associated features [[16]](/library/rCdftH0)

* Fatigue and poor exercise tolerance

* Body pains

* Reduced functional mobility (may negatively impact <u>activities of daily living</u>)

* Clinical features of <u>weight-related complications</u>

---

## Diagnosis

<u>Overweight and obesity in children</u> and <u>overweight and obesity in pregnancy</u> (including <u>preconception care</u>) are addressed separately.




### Approach [[3]](/library/smdtSq0)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[15]](/library/QKXuT_)[[17]](/library/e7Wxk50)




* Address any acute problems and obtain the patient's permission before discussing weight. [[18]](/library/8mdOhq0)[[19]](/library/hGdc_r0)[[20]](/library/iydJUs0)

* Assess <u>BMI classification for overweight and obesity</u>, typically at routine health maintenance visits.

* <u>BMI</u> ≤ 40 kg/m<sup>2</sup>: Perform an anthropometric assessment to confirm that elevated <u>BMI</u> represents excess adiposity.  [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[16]](/library/rCdftH0)

* Perform a clinical evaluation and <u>studies for weight-related complications</u> to assess for:

* <u>Causes of excess adiposity</u>

* <u>Weight-related complications</u>, including <u>metabolic syndrome</u>

* Perform additional studies in select patients as indicated.

* Determine the <u>clinical severity of obesity</u>.





> [!TIP]
> In individuals with <u>BMI</u> > 40 kg/m<sup>2</sup>, excess adiposity can be reasonably assumed without <u>anthropometric measurements</u>. [[16]](/library/rCdftH0)




> [!TIP]
> Screening for <u>metabolic syndrome</u> is performed as part of the routine initial evaluation in patients with <u>obesity</u>. [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)




### Anthropometric assessment [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[15]](/library/QKXuT_)[[16]](/library/rCdftH0)[[21]](/library/8CdOFH0)




The anthropometric assessment for overweight and obesity includes the following:




* Measurements of <u>abdominal obesity</u> [[15]](/library/QKXuT_)[[21]](/library/8CdOFH0)

* <u>Waist circumference</u>

* <u>Waist-to-height ratio</u>

* Assessment for increased or decreased muscle mass and <u>edema</u>

* If <u>physical examination</u> is inconclusive, consider imaging (e.g., <u>DEXA</u>, <u>MRI</u>) to better assess body composition.





### Clinical evaluation [[3]](/library/smdtSq0)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[22]](/library/hudcI70)




The clinical evaluation for overweight and obesity includes a history, review of symptoms, and <u>physical examination</u>.




#### History




* Weight-related history: weight trends, prior attempts at weight loss

* Personal or <u>family history</u> of <u>weight-related complications</u>

* <u>Medications associated with weight gain</u>

* Dietary habits  and level of physical activity

* <u>Social determinants of health</u> that may be barriers to a healthy diet and/or physical activity [[18]](/library/8mdOhq0)

* Experience of weight-related <u>bias</u> and stigma  [[18]](/library/8mdOhq0)





#### Review of symptoms




* <u>Sleep</u>: insufficient <u>sleep</u> time, poor quality of <u>sleep</u>, clinical features of <u>obstructive sleep apnea</u>

* <u>Symptoms of asthma</u>

* <u>Symptoms of hypothyroidism</u>

* <u>Joint</u> or <u>back pain</u>

* <u>Clinical features of GERD</u>

* Psychological conditions: <u>symptoms of depression</u>, <u>anxiety disorders</u>, <u>clinical features of eating disorders</u>

* Female patients: abnormal <u>vaginal bleeding</u>, <u>infertility</u>, <u>urinary incontinence</u>

* Male patients: decreased libido, <u>erectile dysfunction</u>





#### <u>Physical examination</u>




* <u>Vital signs</u>: to assess for <u>bradycardia</u>, <u>tachycardia</u>, <u>elevated blood pressure</u>

* <u>Thyroid examination</u>: to assess for <u>goiter</u> or <u>nodules</u>

* <u>Skin examination</u>: to assess for <u>acanthosis nigricans</u> , <u>hirsutism</u>, <u>skin striae</u>, <u>intertrigo</u>, <u>signs of chronic venous insufficiency</u>, <u>acrochordons</u>

* Female patients: <u>clinical features of PCOS</u>

* Male patients: <u>clinical features of male hypogonadism</u>





> [!TIP]
> Use an appropriately sized blood pressure cuff; extended cuffs may be necessary. [[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)




![Pseudoacanthosis nigricans](media/mscy1n4vw7g3zjujsbtjyt9y.jpg)

Pseudoacanthosis nigricans

![Acrochordons (skin tags)](media/mvni3hakn7f5j59nnef8il2q.jpg)

Acrochordons (skin tags)




### Studies for weight-related complications [[3]](/library/smdtSq0)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[16]](/library/rCdftH0)[[22]](/library/hudcI70)




#### Routine studies




* <u>AST</u> and <u>ALT</u>, and <u>platelets</u>

* <u>Fasting plasma glucose</u> and <u>hemoglobin A1C</u> (see “<u>Diagnostics for diabetes</u>” for interpretation of results)  [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[22]](/library/hudcI70)[[23]](/library/xicEFX0)[[24]](/library/JKdshI0)

* <u>Lipid panel</u>

* Serum <u>creatinine</u> (to calculate <u>estimated GFR</u>)

* May consider obtaining:

* <u>CBC</u>  [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)

* <u>CMP</u>

* <u>Urinalysis</u> and <u>urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio</u>

* <u>ECG</u>





#### Further studies




* Obtain studies to evaluate for <u>weight-related complications</u> based on clinical suspicion, e.g.:

* <u>Diagnostics for hypothyroidism</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for obstructive sleep apnea</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for GERD</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for PCOS</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for amenorrhea</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for male hypogonadism</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for MASLD</u>  [[3]](/library/smdtSq0)[[4]](/library/Fmdghq0)

* History of <u>obesity</u> < 5 years of age and/or early <u>hyperphagia</u>: <u>genetic testing</u> for <u>monogenic disorders</u> or syndromic <u>obesity</u>[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)

---

## Management

<u>Overweight and obesity in children</u> and <u>overweight and obesity in pregnancy</u> (including <u>preconception care</u>) are addressed separately.




### Approach [[3]](/library/smdtSq0)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[15]](/library/QKXuT_)[[16]](/library/rCdftH0)




* Provide collaborative <u>patient-centered care</u>. [[18]](/library/8mdOhq0)[[19]](/library/hGdc_r0)[[20]](/library/iydJUs0)

* Address any acute problems and obtain the patient's permission before discussing weight.

* Focus on specific health outcomes rather than <u>BMI</u> and weight alone.

* Individualize management using <u>shared decision-making</u>.

* Address <u>modifiable risk factors</u>, including:

* <u>Modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease</u>

* Underlying conditions or <u>medications associated with weight gain</u> [[6]](/library/fudkq70)

* Set weight-loss goals.

* <u>Overweight</u> without <u>weight-related complications</u>: maintain or lose weight (based on patient preference)

* All other patients: Long-term weight loss of ≥ 5–15% is recommended.  [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)

* Initiate appropriate interventions.

* All patients: Recommend lifestyle modifications and refer to multidisciplinary specialists as needed.

* <u>Indications for weight-loss medications</u>: Offer pharmacotherapy in addition to lifestyle modifications; use <u>shared decision-making</u> to determine treatment.  [[15]](/library/QKXuT_)[[25]](/library/28WTNM0)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[16]](/library/rCdftH0)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)

* <u>Indications for bariatric surgery</u>: Recommend a <u>bariatric surgery</u> evaluation.

* Provide ongoing management.

* Assess progress toward <u>weight-loss goals</u> and modify therapy as needed.

* Periodically assess other medications for possible dose reduction.  [[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[15]](/library/QKXuT_)

* After long-term weight-loss goal is achieved: Recommend a weight maintenance program for ≥ 1 year. [[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[25]](/library/28WTNM0)





> [!TIP]
> A trial of lifestyle modifications alone is not required before initiating pharmacotherapy in patients with <u>indications for weight-loss medications</u>. [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[16]](/library/rCdftH0)




> [!TIP]
> Loss of ≥ 5% of body weight is considered clinically significant (i.e., decreases the risk or mitigates the effects of some <u>weight-related complications</u>). [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[25]](/library/28WTNM0)

## Lifestyle interventions

### General principles [[3]](/library/smdtSq0)[[6]](/library/fudkq70)[[15]](/library/QKXuT_)




* Lifestyle interventions can lead to weight loss, increase <u>insulin sensitivity</u>, and reduce <u>cardiovascular risk factors</u>.

* To support the implementation of dietary and physical activity changes:

* Refer to a <u>multicomponent behavioral intervention program</u>.

* Address barriers related to <u>social determinants of health</u> (e.g., <u>food insecurity</u>). [[18]](/library/8mdOhq0)

* Lifestyle modifications without pharmacotherapy

* Advise patients on <u>weight-loss goals</u>.

* Initial goal: ≥ 2.5% weight loss at 1 month [[26]](/library/OKXIg_)

* Long-term goal: 5–10% weight loss at 6 months [[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[15]](/library/QKXuT_)

* Base frequency of follow-up on patient need (e.g, every 4–6 weeks initially). [[19]](/library/hGdc_r0)





### Dietary changes [[6]](/library/fudkq70)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[17]](/library/e7Wxk50)




* Provide general <u>counseling on nutrition</u>.

* Various dietary approaches that result in a caloric deficit may be effective for weight loss.

* Refer to a dietitian for specific caloric and energy deficit recommendations.  [[6]](/library/fudkq70)[[15]](/library/QKXuT_)

* Recommend sufficient protein intake during weight loss to prevent muscle loss.

* Most patients: ≥ 1.2 g/kg/day

* Patients with <u>CKD</u>: See "<u>Protein and energy consumption in CKD</u>."





### Physical activity [[6]](/library/fudkq70)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[27]](/library/mBdVYs0)[[28]](/library/ewdx3H0)




* Provide <u>counseling on regular exercise</u>.

* No specific form of physical activity is recommended over another for weight loss.

* Encourage gradually increasing quantity and/or intensity of activity as tolerated to meet recommendations and <u>weight-loss goals</u>.   [[27]](/library/mBdVYs0)[[28]](/library/ewdx3H0)

* Encourage an increase in nonsedentary activities.

* Additional guidance: exercise coach or <u>physical therapy</u> referral





### Behavioral interventions [[6]](/library/fudkq70)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[17]](/library/e7Wxk50)[[25]](/library/28WTNM0)




* Offer referral for to a <u>multicomponent behavioral intervention program</u>, if available.

* Interventions may include:

* Goal setting

* Self-monitoring of weight

* Identification of weight-gain triggers

* Development of self-management skills

* <u>Stress</u> reduction and healthy coping skills

* Support groups and psychological counseling (e.g., <u>cognitive behavioral therapy</u>, intensive <u>behavioral therapy</u>)

* <u>Counseling on sleep hygiene</u>

---

## Pharmacotherapy

### General principles [[5]](/library/jKX_T_)[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[25]](/library/28WTNM0)[[29]](/library/ABdRWs0)




* Offer pharmacotherapy in conjunction with lifestyle modifications to patients with indications for weight-loss medications.

* <u>BMI</u> ≥ 30 kg/m<sup>2</sup>

* <u>BMI</u> ≥ 27 kg/m<sup>2</sup> and at least one <u>weight-related complication</u>

* Choose a medication based on:

* Indications and contraindications

* Patient preference (including cost considerations)

* <u>Weight-loss goals</u>  [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)

* Follow-up

* Frequency: monthly for 3–6 months, and then less frequently  [[6]](/library/fudkq70)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[15]](/library/QKXuT_)

* Titrate medications gradually to improve tolerance.

* Monitor for adverse effects (e.g., <u>cholelithiasis</u> and <u>mood disorders</u>).

* Assess progress toward <u>weight-loss goals</u>, and adjust treatment as needed.

* After 3 months on maximum tolerated dose: If weight loss is < 5%, change to an alternative medication.[[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)[[25]](/library/28WTNM0)

* Long-term: If not meeting individualized goals, consider changing to an alternative medication and/or referral to an <u>obesity</u> specialist.

* Long-term use of medications is typically required for sustained weight loss.

[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)[[31]](/library/kAdmPs0)<br><br>* Monitor for adverse effects (e.g., <u>pancreatitis</u>, <u>gallbladder</u> disease, <u>malnutrition</u>, and <u>sarcopenia</u>). [[31]](/library/kAdmPs0)<br><br><br> |
| Centrally acting medications | <br><br>* For long-term use<br><br>* <u>Naltrexone</u>/<u>bupropion</u> extended release DOSAGE [[25]](/library/28WTNM0)<br><br>* <u>Phentermine/topiramate extended release</u> DOSAGE [[25]](/library/28WTNM0)<br><br>* For use ≤ 12 weeks  <br><br>* <u>Phentermine</u> DOSAGE [[25]](/library/28WTNM0)<br><br>* <u>Diethylpropion</u> DOSAGE [[25]](/library/28WTNM0)<br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Naltrexone</u>/<u>bupropion</u><br><br>* <u>Depression</u><br><br>* <u>Smoking cessation</u><br><br>* <u>Phentermine</u>/<u>topiramate</u> <br><br>* <u>Migraines</u><br><br>* <u>Binge eating disorder</u><br><br>* Second-line option for <u>T2DM</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Periodically monitor blood pressure and <u>heart rate</u>.<br><br>* <u>Naltrexone</u>/<u>bupropion</u>: Avoid taking with fatty meals; use caution with <u>beta blockers</u>.  [[10]](/library/-bVDwG0)<br><br>* <u>Phentermine</u>/<u>topiramate</u> must be tapered when discontinuing.  [[25]](/library/28WTNM0)<br><br>* Check state laws for prescribing requirements for <u>phentermine</u> and <u>diethylpropion</u>.<br><br><br> |
| <u>Lipase</u> inhibitors | <br>* <u>Orlistat</u><br><br> | <br>* Not routinely recommended; may be selected based on patient preference   [[25]](/library/28WTNM0)<br><br> | <br>* Advise patients to:<br><br>* Take with meals containing fat.<br><br>* Take a daily multivitamin including <u>fat-soluble vitamins</u> (2 hours apart from taking <u>orlistat</u>).<br><br> |





> [!WARNING]
> Due to the <u>teratogenicity</u> risk, advise patients who can become pregnant to use <u>contraception</u> while taking <u>pharmacotherapy for obesity</u>. [[6]](/library/fudkq70)[[25]](/library/28WTNM0)[[32]](/library/tmdXhq0)




> [!TIP]
> <u>Tirzepatide</u> has the highest <u>efficacy</u> in terms of total weight loss compared to other <u>weight-loss drugs</u>.[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)




> [!NOTE]
> <u>Orlistat</u> reversibly inhibits gastric and <u>pancreatic lipase</u>, resulting in a decrease in fat breakdown and absorption, and can cause gastrointestinal side effects.

---

## Metabolic and bariatric surgery

* <u>Indications for bariatric surgery</u> [[33]](/library/08WeOM0)

* <u>Class 2 obesity</u> or <u>class 3 obesity</u>

* <u>Class 1 obesity</u> with either of the following:

* <u>T2DM</u>

* Lack of improvement following nonsurgical interventions

* Average weight loss with <u>bariatric surgery</u>: > 20% [[6]](/library/fudkq70)[[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)

* See “<u>Bariatric surgery</u>” for additional information.

---

## Complications

* Cardiometabolic [[34]](/library/9tdNf70)

* <u>Hypertension</u>, cardiovascular disease (<u>ASCVD</u>)

* <u>Atrial fibrillation</u>

* <u>Cardiomyopathy</u> and <u>congestive heart failure</u>  [[35]](/library/MKXMS_)[[36]](/library/7KX43_)

* <u>Insulin resistance</u>: <u>prediabetes</u>, <u>T2DM</u>

* <u>Dyslipidemia</u>

* <u>PCOS</u>

* <u>MASLD</u>, <u>MASH</u>: increased risk of <u>liver cirrhosis</u> and <u>liver</u> <u>malignancy</u>

* Respiratory

* <u>Obstructive sleep apnea</u> (<u>OSA</u>)

* <u>Obesity hypoventilation syndrome</u>

* <u>Asthma</u>  [[26]](/library/OKXIg_)

* Musculoskeletal

* <u>Osteoarthritis</u>

* <u>Chronic back pain</u> [[37]](/library/9ydNhs0)

* <u>Slipped capital femoral epiphysis</u> and <u>Blount disease</u> (especially in children) [[4]](/library/Fmdghq0)

* Reproductive and genitourinary [[38]](/library/yBddWs0)

* <u>Chronic kidney disease</u>  [[35]](/library/MKXMS_)

* Menstrual dysfunction and/or <u>ovulatory dysfunction</u>

* <u>Adverse events</u> during <u>pregnancy</u>: e.g., <u>gestational hypertension</u>, <u>preterm labor</u>, and <u>pregnancy loss</u> (see “<u>Overweight and obesity in pregnancy</u>”) [[39]](/library/pKXLh_)

* <u>Urinary incontinence</u>

* <u>Infertility</u> [[13]](/library/Exd8yH0)

* <u>Erectile dysfunction</u> [[40]](/library/k6XmO_)

* <u>Male hypogonadism</u>

* Gastrointestinal [[41]](/library/U2cbSb0)

* <u>Cholelithiasis</u>, <u>cholecystitis</u>

* <u>GERD</u>

* <u>Colonic diverticulosis</u>

* Malignancies  [[42]](/library/HKXK3_)[[43]](/library/d6XoP_)

* <u>Hepatocellular carcinoma</u>

* <u>Colorectal cancer</u>

* <u>Breast cancer</u>

* <u>Endometrial cancer</u>

* <u>Renal cancer</u> [[44]](/library/QuduI70)

* <u>CNS</u>

* <u>Idiopathic intracranial hypertension</u>

* <u>Dementia</u>

* Psychological [[18]](/library/8mdOhq0)

* <u>Anxiety</u>

* <u>Depression</u>

* Internalized weight <u>bias</u> and/or stigma

* <u>Eating disorders</u>

* Other

* Disability causing limitation of <u>activities of daily living</u>

* Inflammatory <u>skin</u> diseases, <u>intertrigo</u>

* <u>Lymphedema</u>

* <u>Thromboembolism</u>, including <u>portal vein thrombosis</u>  [[45]](/library/jla_9k)[[46]](/library/h5XcPA)

* <u>Gout</u> [[47]](/library/zGbrbv)





> [!TIP]
> The co-occurence of <u>central obesity</u>, <u>T2DM</u> or <u>prediabetes</u>, <u>hypertension</u>, and <u>dyslipidemia</u> is known as <u>metabolic syndrome</u>. [[48]](/library/Z3aZS4)




We list the most important complications. The selection is not exhaustive.
